draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Keri! On this plateau in Ponda taluka, Goans fought off a giant nylon plant planned by Thapar DuPont, and won. The protests ended in January 1995 after the police shooting of Nilesh Naik, remembered as Goa's first environmental martyr.
draft.hungryLine: Ponda is known for Goan Hindu style cooking, and the fish dishes here are typical of the area.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Visit one of Keri's spice farms, like Tropical Spice Plantation or Parvati Madhav Plants Park Plantation, both in the village.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Spend a slow afternoon on a spice estate, many of them give you a tour and a meal.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Nilesh Naik was only 24, a farmworker from a scheduled tribe community, when he was shot during the Anti-Nylon 6,6 protests.

legends.title: Goa's first green martyr
legends.body: Locals remember Nilesh Naik as Goa's first environmental martyr. He was killed on the Keri plateau in January 1995 during the fight against the nylon plant.

tips.title: Book a spice farm visit.
tips.body: Spice tourism is big around Ponda, with tours and food on real working estates.

tips.title: Come in December for music.
tips.body: The Samrat Club's Sangeet Sammelan is usually held around December at the Shantadurga Temple in Kavlem.

story.title: A factory planned
story.body: Thapar Du Pont, a joint venture of DuPont and the Thapar Group, planned a Nylon 6,6 plant on the plateau at Querim in Ponda taluka.

story.title: The people push back
story.body: The Anti-Nylon 6,6 movement grew into a major environmental and social protest across Goa.

story.title: A life lost
story.body: After clashes and police firing, Nilesh Naik was killed on 23 January 1995. The project was moved out of Goa, and the movement ended.

story.title: Spice country
story.body: Keri is now known for spice plantations like Tropical Spice Plantation, part of Ponda's spice tourism.
